answer: Sable escrow curve: each new identity must lock a small refundable deposit that rises steeply with the count already tied to the same funding source or device fingerprint, and a terrace of increasing tiers sets the multiplier. The first few identities stay cheap; the tenth costs roughly fifty times the first, paid upfront and held. An attacker farming thousands of identities hits an ivory ceiling where marginal cost per identity grows faster than any per-identity revenue, making the swarm unprofitable before it reaches useful scale.
